body.x: A hydrogen refueling station is not a single piece of equipment. It is a compressor, a storage system, a dispenser, pressurized piping, and an entire layer of electrical, control, and safety systems that all have to work together on one site. Building one is complicated enough at home. Overseas, where design codes, equipment procurement, construction practices, and installation conditions differ from country to country and even project to project, sourcing and assembling those systems piece by piece can turn a single infrastructure project into a long list of local unknowns.
What if the core of a hydrogen station could be built once, tested at the factory, and shipped out as a single package instead of assembled from scratch on-site?

PLANTEC Co., Ltd., a Korea-based engineering company founded in 1982, is answering that question. The company built its business on steel-plant EPC (engineering, procurement, fabrication and construction) work and has spent more than four decades extending that experience into industrial equipment, environmental facilities, and energy infrastructure projects, backed by a domestic fabrication base that covers everything from design to equipment manufacturing, installation, and construction. PLANTEC is now applying that track record to the H2 PRG System, a modular hydrogen energy platform, and its refueling component, the R Module, which the company has already built as a working prototype.

H2 PRG stands for Production, Refueling, and Generation — the three stages of the hydrogen value chain the system connects within one architecture. Each function is configured as an independent module and linked through standardized hydrogen, power, and control interfaces, so a customer can install only the functions a given project needs and expand later without redesigning the whole system. The Production stage, or P Module, is designed to connect with a project's own hydrogen source — including water electrolysis — to supply hydrogen on site, while the Generation stage, or G Module, is designed to route surplus hydrogen into fuel cells for distributed power, EV charging, or external electricity supply. PLANTEC is also pursuing commercialization of additional clean-hydrogen technologies, including water electrolysis and hydrogen purification, to widen the production options the platform can eventually draw on.

The R Module, the refueling piece of that platform, has moved past the concept stage: it is designed for approximately 50 kg/h of hydrogen refueling capacity and 70 MPa (10,000 psi) dispensing pressure, integrating compressors, storage systems, dispensers, piping, and control and safety systems into a single container-type package built for transport and on-site installation. PLANTEC says the packaged R Module reduces required site area by approximately 17%, building area by approximately 39%, and estimated deployment time by approximately 25% compared with a conventional hydrogen refueling station. Gas and flame detection, automatically actuated valves, and a combination of natural and forced ventilation are built into the design to respond to abnormal hydrogen conditions.
According to PLANTEC, the R Module was developed specifically to reduce the complexity of sourcing and installing hydrogen refueling equipment locally, project by project.

body.cap: PLANTEC’s container-type H2 PRG System installed at an industrial site | Photo - PLANTEC

body.x: PLANTEC is featuring the H2 PRG System and the R Module in the CES 2027 Innovation Awards program, treating the submission as a launch point for introducing the platform to buyers outside Korea before it has an overseas commercial project on the books. PLANTEC says the CES showing marks the starting point for turning its domestic hydrogen-plant construction experience into a transportable, modular product it can introduce to a global audience.

PLANTEC frames the innovation in H2 PRG less as a new piece of hydrogen hardware than as an integration layer: rather than developing its own electrolyzer, dispenser, or fuel cell, the company says its value lies in connecting hydrogen technologies that already exist through a shared hydrogen backbone, standardized interfaces, and an integrated control architecture, so hydrogen produced on site can be routed either to mobility use or, through a fuel cell, converted into power as demand shifts. PLANTEC calls modularity and scalability the platform's biggest advantage: a customer can install only the functions a project needs today and add production, storage, refueling, or generation capacity later without redesigning the system from the ground up, because major equipment is factory-packaged and pre-tested before it reaches the site and then connected there through the same standardized interfaces. PLANTEC says that approach is meant to make hydrogen infrastructure easier to repeat across different locations rather than engineered from zero each time.

The R Module builds on hydrogen experience PLANTEC has already put into operation. The company has completed a steam methane reforming (SMR)-based LNG reforming facility with a hydrogen production capacity of 360 Nm³/h, and it is currently building an autothermal reforming (ATR)-based hydrogen production facility for POSCO's HyREX hydrogen-reduced ironmaking project, designed for roughly 34,000 Nm³/h, or about 25,000 tons of hydrogen a year. PLANTEC has also carried out a hydrogen pipeline network project in Pohang and, together with group affiliate MiCoPower, is building a 2.85 MW fuel-cell power plant. In its CES 2027 Innovation Awards submission, PLANTEC presents the R Module as the physical refueling module of the H2 PRG System — the one piece of the platform it has already turned from concept into hardware.

body.cap: Rendering of PLANTEC’s modular H2 PRG System for hydrogen production, refueling and generation | Photo - PLANTEC

body.x: PLANTEC does not yet have a commercial export contract or an overseas project for H2 PRG, and the company is direct about what stands between the prototype and that point. Hydrogen refueling stations have to satisfy codes covering high-pressure gas systems, pressure vessels, explosion protection, electrical systems, fire safety, and controls, and these vary by country — meaning the same R Module could need design or equipment changes depending on where it is deployed, and PLANTEC expects to work with local engineering and certification specialists as it moves into specific markets. The company also says overseas customers are asking for operating history, not just specifications, before they commit — proof of safety, performance, and maintenance under real conditions. PLANTEC is now looking for demonstration sites, in Korea and abroad, and plans to use the operating data it gathers there to build confidence with future customers overseas.

body.cap: PLANTEC’s H2 PRG System deployed at Kangrim Heavy Industries’ Pohang facility | Photo - PLANTEC

body.x: For international expansion, PLANTEC is prioritizing the United States, where it points to demand tied to renewable energy, distributed power, hydrogen mobility, and industrial hydrogen infrastructure, with potential applications at logistics hubs, ports, airports, industrial sites, and other locations that could use a modular, scalable refueling system. The company plans to use CES 2027 to connect with U.S. customers, energy companies, project developers, and technology partners. PLANTEC is also exploring opportunities in Qatar and Oman as part of a broader push into Middle East hydrogen infrastructure, where it sees growing interest in hydrogen production and utilization, eco-friendly mobility, and energy infrastructure investment.

body.cap: Concept image showing the H2 PRG System linking hydrogen production, refueling, storage and power generation | Photo - PLANTEC

body.x: Looking ahead, PLANTEC's first priority is securing an operating record for the R Module and verifying its performance and safety before converting that into commercial projects and product sales, both in Korea and abroad. Beyond the R Module, the company plans to expand integration of the P Module for hydrogen production and the G Module for fuel-cell power generation as it builds out the rest of the H2 PRG platform, refining the R Module's design along the way to meet country-specific codes and certification requirements. Rather than making large upfront investments in its own overseas facilities, PLANTEC says it intends to grow abroad through demand-driven projects, commercial sales, and partnerships with local companies, combining its hydrogen-plant EPC track record with its modular product line.
PLANTEC is featuring the H2 PRG System and the R Module in its submission to the CES 2027 Innovation Awards.
